sections.title: Sound of the letter O
paragraphs: The letter is named (O) /oʊ/. Its main sound is a vowel heard in (ox) /ɑks/, which means ox. A vowel is a sound made with open air. This letter makes four sounds in total. Each sound depends on the word.

sections.title: How to say the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw and pull your tongue low and back. For the second sound, start mid and back, then round your lips into a small circle. For the third sound, keep your tongue resting in the middle. For the fourth sound, lift your tongue high in the back and make a tight circle with your lips. Touch your throat to feel each voiced vowel vibrate.

sections.title: Spelling rules for the sounds
paragraphs: In closed stressed syllables, this vowel sounds like /ɑ/, as in (hot) /hɑt/. In open syllables or before a silent e, it sounds like /oʊ/, as in (go) /ɡoʊ/ and (home) /hoʊm/. In unstressed syllables, it becomes a schwa, as in (lemon) /lɛ.mən/ and (atom) /æ.təm/. A schwa is a short, weak vowel in the middle of the mouth. In some common words, it sounds like /uː/, as in (do) /duː/ and (move) /muːv/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not replace the diphthong in (go) /ɡoʊ/ with a flat, single vowel. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second. Start open and finish with round lips. Do not pronounce unstressed vowels clearly in (lemon) /lɛ.mən/. Relax your mouth completely on that weak beat.
